research_mode: official MHCLG, ONS, Office for Statistics Regulation, Home Office and Police.uk web sources only; methodology, quality, freshness, completeness, geography and statistical-status guards; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.name: English indices of deprivation 2025 technical report
verified_claims: published 30 October 2025
IoD25 measures relative deprivation in lower-layer super output areas
the report documents the conceptual framework, domain methodology, design principles, quality assurance and component indicators
limitations: the technical report is methodology evidence and not a parcel result
runtime still requires the corrected v2 artifact and an exact one-LSOA spatial join

sources.name: The quality of police recorded crime statistics for England and Wales
verified_claims: published 16 May 2024 and updated 3 March 2025
police recorded crime is official statistics rather than accredited official statistics
for many crime types it is a better indicator of police activity than trends in crime while CSEW is the better source for long-term trends in crimes covered by the survey
limitations: recorded-crime counts cannot be treated as a complete measure of crime incidence
source-role differences must remain explicit in any candidate evidence

sources.name: Police force recording accuracy findings and inspection limits
verified_claims: HMICFRS estimated 92.4 percent recording accuracy for all crime excluding fraud by the end of its 2021 to 2022 programme
17 of 23 inspected forces recorded more than 90 percent and six more than 95 percent
inspections use a subset of recent crimes and occur every three to five years
limitations: inspection accuracy is a point-in-time force snapshot rather than current monthly assurance
a force percentage does not establish exact parcel attribution confidence

sources.name: Police recorded crime quality improvement framework
verified_claims: OSR identifies insufficient Home Office oversight as a significant quality risk
it recommends more consistent force quality assurance and better understanding of crime-recording IT systems
it recommends that ONS explain reliability assessments by offence type
limitations: regulatory recommendations are quality-governance evidence rather than direct crime measurement
they do not produce a parcel score

sources.name: Developing a Crime Severity Score for England and Wales
verified_claims: the score was designed to complement police recorded crime and support expert analysis of police demand
offence weights are derived primarily from sentencing information
the measure is affected by differences in crime-recording practices over time and between areas
limitations: the score is an analytical severity measure and not a safety probability
the published tool operates at police-force-area and regional levels rather than parcel level

sources.name: Guide to finding crime statistics
verified_claims: the guide was revised on 7 April 2026
police recorded crime is available by Police Force Area and Community Safety Partnership
CSEW open tables provide incidence, prevalence and perception breakdowns by region and demographics
limitations: PFA and CSP products are broader than LSOAs and parcels
regional survey breakdowns cannot be assigned to an exact property

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Crime data last-updated API contract
verified_claims: crime data in the API is updated once a month
the endpoint returns the month of the latest crime data in ISO date format
the documented example reports 2026-05-01 and states that the day component is not meaningful
limitations: the latest global month does not prove that every force supplied complete data
force-level completeness must also be checked against the changelog

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: data.police.uk changelog and known issues
verified_claims: the May 2026 changelog records missing crime submissions for multiple forces including British Transport Police, Gloucestershire, Greater Manchester and Lincolnshire
the changelog separately records later refreshes and missing stop-and-search submissions
known issues include force IT-system and geocoding problems
limitations: availability and corrections vary by force and month
a global API response must not be interpreted as uniform national completeness

sources.name: Police recorded crime and outcomes open data tables user guide
verified_claims: updated 30 January 2025
police recorded crime time series can be materially affected by recording policy and practice and the 2002 to 2003 NCRS change creates a discontinuity
the tables identify PFA or CSP, period and offence code and monthly anomalies are returned to forces for validation or correction
limitations: table rows are area-period-offence counts rather than exact incident or parcel observations
comparisons require recording-policy, geography and reference-table version controls

sources.name: Home Office Crime Recording Rules for frontline officers and staff
verified_claims: the page was last updated on 16 July 2026
the rules provide a national standard for recording and counting notifiable offences in England and Wales
the page records multiple 2026 rule and outcomes-framework updates
limitations: recording rules standardise classification and counting but do not provide exact incident coordinates
rule versions must be pinned when interpreting changes in recorded counts

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk monthly data archive
verified_claims: archive files provide a complete snapshot of crime, outcome and stop-and-search data as held at a particular point in history
a latest archive is published monthly
historical archives allow an analysis to pin the source snapshot used
limitations: a complete archive snapshot can still contain force-specific omissions documented in the changelog
archive completeness is not exact parcel-location accuracy

sources.publisher: Police.uk / Single Online Home National Digital Team
sources.name: Police.uk open data statistical-status notice
verified_claims: the page centralises data publications on behalf of police forces
it states that the data should not be considered official statistics
it describes the data as an indication only of current force performance at publication time
limitations: street-level open data cannot inherit accredited-statistics status
indicative force-performance data must not be promoted to an exact parcel safety probability
